public_rationale: The FTC report released January 17, 2025 expressly makes no assessment of whether anyone engaged in illegal conduct [e1]. Washington Technology's August 21, 2025 article reports Ask Sage's allegations that government agreements misled agencies about costs and capabilities [e2]. The article does not establish coordinated cost deception by OpenAI and Anthropic [e2]. Neither item establishes or affirmatively disproves the alleged coordination, its claimed customer effects, or the claimed transition to cost-covering billing [e1, e2].
limitations: The FTC report does not resolve the specific allegation of coordinated cost deception [e1].
The procurement article reports allegations rather than substantiated findings of coordination or resulting customer deception [e2].
Neither item supplies matched provider-cost and contract records establishing when charges covered costs [e1, e2].

public_payload.normalized_proposition: OpenAI, Anthropic and other AI companies actively conspired to mislead the world about AI's true costs, and this worked well until they decided to try charging what AI actually costs.

statement.excerpt: OpenAI, Anthropic and other AI companies have actively conspired to mislead the world about the true costs of AI, and it was working great right up until they decided to try charging what it actually cost.

from_speaker: OpenAI, Anthropic and other AI companies
mislead the world about the true costs of AI
our_interpretation: The plain reading alleges knowing coordination between companies to deceive customers about costs, not merely similar pricing strategies or independent promotional claims.
The claim also alleges that the deception succeeded and ended when companies attempted cost-covering billing.
The surrounding references to the last few years and Q1 2026 billing changes place the alleged conduct in the period approximately June 2022 through the post.
This is principally an allegation about coordinated conduct and intent, rather than a specified financial amount.
criteria.support_condition: Authenticated communications, admissions, or substantiated investigative findings establish coordinated cost deception involving the named companies, customer deception resulting from it, and the claimed transition to attempted cost-covering charges.
criteria.contradiction_condition: A sufficiently comprehensive documentary record or substantiated investigation affirmatively disproves the alleged coordination or establishes that the claimed deception and billing sequence did not occur.

evidence.locator: Cover-page disclaimer; Executive Summary describes the study's scope
evidence.publisher: Federal Trade Commission, Office of Technology
evidence.explanation: The primary regulatory report examines Microsoft–OpenAI, Amazon–Anthropic, and Google–Anthropic partnerships and potential competition concerns. It supplies no finding establishing the alleged cost-deception conspiracy, and its disclaimer also prevents treating it as exoneration.

evidence.locator: Article standfirst; subsequent discussion of the procurement protests
evidence.explanation: This reports a competitor's procurement protests and concerns about how government agreements were presented. It is evidence of an allegation, not a finding of coordination, successful worldwide deception, or subsequent cost-covering billing; the underlying protest was not obtained.

public_payload.what_would_resolve: Authenticated communications or substantiated investigative findings establishing or affirmatively disproving the alleged coordination, plus evidence of customer effects and dated billing records matched to defined provider costs to test the claimed sequence through June 2, 2026.
